2 for the death of Mr.G.S.Phanibabu and for the injuries sustained by the petitioner Mr.Raghavendra Rao P. in a road traffic accident dated 23.07.2020.  2. The case of the Petitioners in both the cases  is that:
 On 23.07.2020 at about 7.15pm Mr.G.S.Phanibabu was driving the Car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB9938 and Mr.Raghavendra Rao P. was an inmate in the same car and they were proceeding on Nice Road, carefully and cautiously, observing all the traffic rules and regulations. 
When they reached near Anjanapura Lake, Bangalore, the right side front tyre of the Car was punctured. Hence,
G.S.Phanibabu parked the Car on the left side of the road by putting all the Car parking lights. Both alighted from the Car, put safety stones around the car. After taking all the safety measures, they started changing the punctured tyre as pedestrians. At that time, all of a sudden the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human  5 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020  SCCH - 25 life from BG Road towards Kengeri side without blowing horn or giving any type of signal, lost control of his Raghavendra Rao. P vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6869582/
3 motorcycle and hit Mr.G.S.Phanibabu and Mr.Raghavendra Rao and fell down. Due to tremendous impact,
Mr.G.S.Phanibabu (in MVC 2854/2020) sustained multiple severe accidental injuries and died on the way to the hospital and Mr.Raghavendra Rao (in MVC 2855/2020) also sustained multiple severe accidental injuries on his head region, chest region, hands and other parts of the body. 
 3. It is the further case of the Petitioners (in MVC No.2854/2020) that, immediately G.S.Phanibabu was shifted to Vijayashree hospital, Bangalore and death was confirmed in the hospital. Post mortem was done on 25.07.2020 at KIMS Hospital & Research Centre and dead body was handed over to his family. Prior to the accident,
deceased G.S.Phanibabu was working as a National Sales & Business Development manager (Food) at ALS Testing  6 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020  SCCH - 25 Services India Private Limited, Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.14,36,255/ per annum. He was also working as a Chief Advisor at Trans Tools Corporation, Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.12,24,000/ per annum. Hence,
his total income is Rs.26,60,255/ per annum from both the companies. Prior to the accident, the deceased G.S.Phanibabu was hale and healthy, the only bread earner of the entire family. Due to his sudden death the deceased's wife and children have been deprived of the Raghavendra Rao. 4 contribution which the deceased was making towards the entire family. So far, they have spent Rs.1,00,000/

It is the further case of the Petitioner (in MVC No.2855/2020) that, immediately he was shifted Astar Super Specialty hospital, Bangalore, admitted as an inpatient, treated from 23.07.2020 to 25.07.2020 for the  7 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020  SCCH - 25 injuries and discharged with advice. So far he has spent Rs.80,000/ towards treatment, medicines, nourishment and conveyance etc., At the time of accident the petitioner was working as a Project Manager at ALS Testing Services India Private Limited and earning a sum of Rs.95,000/
per month. Due to accidental injuries he was not able to attend to his Job regularly. So, he lost that income. 
 5. Therefore, the Respondents 1 & 2 being the insurer and the Owner of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to them. Hence this petition. 
 6. In response to service of notice issued by this court/Tribunal, the Respondent No.1 has appeared and filed written statement. In spite of due service of summons,
the Respondent No.2 did not appear in MVC 2854/2020.

5  8 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020  SCCH - 25 Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel but did not chose to file written statement. 
 7. Objection of the Respondent No.1.
 The respondent No.1/Insurance Company admitted issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and stated that it is valid from 31.10.2019 to 30.10.2020. This respondent denied the alleged accident, manner of accident and contended that insured vehicle is falsely implicated. Further the respondent No.1 has willfully handed over the possession of the vehicle to such person/rider who was not having valid and effective DL as on the date of accident. 
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. 
The present claim petitions are bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties. Further the alleged accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself. 
Further the Respondent No.1 denied the age, income,

 The Petitioners in both the cases in order to substantiate that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590, have got examined petitioner No.1 in MVC No.2854/2020 as PW.1 and Petitioner himself in MVC No.2855/2020 as PW.2 and produced 9 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.9. In the cross examination of RW.1 it is elicited that the respondent No.2 had DL to drive Two wheeler as on the date of accident. 
Therefore, from the crossexamination of Pws.1 and 2 and evidence of RW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disprove the alleged manner of accident and hence the defence of the respondent No.1 that there was negligence on the part of the deceased is not acceptable.
 13. Further, the FIR, FIS, spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, MVA report, Inquest Mahazar, PM report, charge sheet and death certificate produced by the Petitioners as per Exs.P.1 to P.9 are public documents which are issued  16 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020  SCCH - 25 by a public office and they have got presumptive value under law. As such, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 and documents produced by them. The counsel for the petitioner has relied on (1) 2009 (II) ACC 444 Supreme Court of India: Bimladevi & Ors.

And (3). 2021 ACJ 17 Supreme Court of India: Anita Sharma & Ors. Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. &
Anr., wherein the courts have held that the claimants have to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability. Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PWs.1 and 2 coupled with documents produced by them this court is of the opinion that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05KE5590 has ridden the same in a rash and  17 MVC No.2854 and 2855/2020  SCCH - 25 negligent manner, endangering human life, came with high speed and dashed against the deceased G.S.Phanibabu and the petitioner Raghavendra Rao P. and caused the accident, as a result of which both have sustained grievous injuries, due to which G.S.Phanibabu succumbed to the injuries on the way to the hospital. Accordingly Issue No.1 in MVC No.2855/2020 and Issue No.2 in MVC No.2854/2020 are held in the affirmative.
